subject: people
objective: Summarize the survey scores with the design weights
instruction: A business is preparing a people & organisation analysis. The question is: Summarize the survey scores with the design weights. The tile covers Summarise scores with the design weights you supply, stating the weighting rule. The declared figures are: values 1, 2, 3, 4; weights 1, 1, 1, 3; weight kind reliability. Use weighted summary in a competitive market and industry context, and report the method's result.

result._appendix: {'weight_kind': 'reliability', 'definitions': {'weighted_mean': 'sum(w*x) / sum(w)', 'reliability_sd': 'sqrt( sum(w*(x-mean)^2) / (sum(w) - sum(w^2)/sum(w)) )  [unbiased under reliability weights]', 'frequency_sd': 'sqrt( sum(w*(x-mean)^2) / (sum(w) - 1) )  [frequency weights count observations]', 'n_eff': 'sum(w)^2 / sum(w^2)  [effective sample size]', 'design_effect': 'n / n_eff'}, 'inference': 'None is provided. No standard error, confidence interval or test is computed, because that needs a declared complex design (stratification, clustering, replicate weights).'}
result._checks: [('second_implementation_agrees', True, 'float route agrees with the Decimal route'), ('equal_weights_reproduce_the_unweighted_summary', True, 'unit weights are the ordinary sample summary'), ('mean_is_invariant_to_weight_scaling', True, 'multiplying every weight by a constant leaves the mean unchanged'), ('larger_values_weighted_more_raise_the_mean', True, 'extra weight on values farther above the minimum moves the mean upward'), ('design_effect_is_one_for_equal_weights', True, 'equal weights give an effective sample size equal to n')]
